title: Writing the Courier column and travelling for a liquor company
summary: Tex describes filling in for Butch Curry, how to build a column, and his road work for a liquor company across Louisiana and Texas.

blocks.x: Mm-hmm . Mm-hmm . I guess you could say writers for black newspapers alive today other than John Russo for any extended period of time. And Butch was going out of town or going someplace, and he asked me to do this article. I think he was ill at that time. And so I had just come off a road trip. I don't know, I just had some time off. Have you ever done a column before? Yeah, because I had written columns for the Informer Sentinel, which was a very large newspaper. That was another newspaper that we got off the front of find. Yeah, well, I think I have some columns I've written, and I think I have one or two sheets of the old Informer Sentinel. Carter Wesley was the owner out of Houston, Texas, who owned the old Informer Sentinel. Because at that time, you had the Pittsburgh career. You had the Louisiana Weekly and the Informer Sentinel. Here in New Orleans, and everybody was doing some business. But at that time, the papers were five cents apiece. So that's a different thing. And I think that's what it's going to cause me to be. But Butch Kerr was ill that week, I think.
When you're putting a column like this together, what do you have to do to put a column? It looks like a lot of work, is what I'm saying.

What do you have to do to put a column? Well, in doing a column like that, number one, you have to be what is known in newspaper reports. You have to be on the scene. You have to have connections. You have to know people. And you have to get involved. And you have to ask questions. You know, like I raised my kids. I said, well, God gave us two hands, but I'm going to use one. And I'm going to educate you, and you never have to come back to me for many questions and answers. Who, what, where, why, and when. When you answer these questions, you know the answer to everything. But there's another letter, which is very important, which is affiliated with the who, what, why, and when. It's how. Who, what, where, why, and when. And then mathematically or geometrically or scientifically, if you can answer these questions, you know this is how Edison and the big scientists and these guys, that's the way they operate, or who, what, where, why, and when, and how.
So you must have been out all night.

No, I had traveled quite a bit. See, at that time, I was working for a brown, brown, see, that was a liquor company. You know, this old, old Forrester, and early times, and King Liquor at that time. And I used to travel all through Louisiana and part of Texas. If you notice, I have a lot, a lot about Texas in here, about, well, Forrestal, what is the name, Rosenthal out of Orange, Texas, who was a big time promoter. He and Frank Pannier, they were co-promoters on shows from New Orleans all the way over to Orange, Texas. So this is how I started writing this thing when Butch asked me to do it, because, you see, I was either in Lafayette, Louisiana, either I was in Hopalooza, Louisiana, or either I was in Orange, Texas, either I was in Houston, Texas, or either I was in, I didn't go up to Dallas, but Beaumont, and the home of Louisiana, you name it, I was all in these different areas, even on the West Bank of the River where my cousin Lloyd Spencer had Lloyd's Esquire line. This is where all the good looking women in Jefferson, Georgia, and all the guys were... All the guys were...
